items.title: Context Matters for Tech Use and Development
items.abstract: This chapter examines everyday digital practices on the Cape Flats. Through ethnographic engagement with residents and tech entrepreneurs, we demonstrate how context matters in understanding the importance of the phone as critical social infrastructure amid poverty, violence, and uneven connectivity. We ask whose rights to connectivity, privacy, and transparency in data collection are considered. The chapter analyzes barriers to access in the digital economy and why developing tech from the Cape Flats matters in breaking stereotypes about people from the area. We consider much-needed initiatives in terms of solving local problems with tech, while querying the awkward promises of the Silicon Cape, situating findings within broader debates on sociotechnical imaginaries, classification, and algorithmic bias. We argue that understanding tech and energy futures requires sustained attention to context, place-based inequality, racialization, and historical dispossession. Data is the business model for tech startups and tech giants alike. With a mobile phone in the pocket and across “smart technologies,” data is generated, stored, and shared—often in opaque ways—as the commodification of everyday interactions turns life into data. We ground this discussion and consider the everyday realities and material conditions that tech responds to—solving or augmenting the issues depending on viewpoint.

items.title: Contrastive Activation-Guided Zeroth-Order Preference Optimisation for Memory-Efficient LLM Alignment
items.abstract: Direct Preference Optimisation (DPO) simplifies reinforcement learning from human feedback, but still relies on traditional backpropagation and its associated activation-memory cost. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimisation avoids backpropagation, yet isotropic perturbations can produce noisy updates for preference objectives defined by differences between chosen and rejected responses. We introduce Contrastive Activation-guided Zeroth-Order Direct Preference Optimisation (CA-ZODPO), which constructs a low-rank search subspace from the activation discrepancy between the chosen and rejected responses in each preference pair. Perturbations are restricted to this subspace, while momentum is maintained in low-rank coordinates to preserve the memory advantages of ZO training. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with Anthropic HH-RLHF, CA-ZODPO outperforms common ZO baselines and remains competitive with first-order DPO in pairwise preference evaluation. It also reduces peak GPU memory by about 59\% at a sequence length of 2048 while retaining the sequence-length scaling behaviour of zeroth-order training.

items.title: CP-Agent: A harness-engineered agent for crystal plasticity simulation workflows
items.abstract: Crystal plasticity (CP) simulations are widely used to predict the mechanical behavior of polycrystalline metals, yet their routine application remains hindered by the substantial manual effort of configuring heterogeneous tools, orchestrating multi-step data pipelines, and calibrating constitutive parameters against experimental measurements. These bottlenecks impede productivity in systematic parameter studies, motivating growing interest in automated workflow solutions. This study presents CP-Agent , a harness-engineered LLM-based agent that autonomously executes complete CP modeling workflows from tasks specified in natural language. Operating under the ReAct paradigm, the agent reasons about tool selection and sequencing while delegating numerical search to established optimizers. The harness comprises a minimal system prompt, typed tool definitions, a dispatcher, and a safety-bounded iteration loop, encoding domain knowledge through tool schemas rather than hard-coded logic. CP-Agent is demonstrated on four case studies: calibrating four slip parameters of additively manufactured stainless steel 316L against tensile data; validating the workflow against published copper benchmarks, reproducing stress–strain and texture evolution; recovering the initial crystallographic texture of copper, where the agent correctly identifies a diffuse initial texture; and reproducing the multi-pass rolling texture evolution of a Mg-Zn-Ca alloy, where the agent chains five deformation passes and recovers the experimentally observed weakened, split basal texture. In all cases, the agent inferred the correct execution sequence from the task statement, robustly across repeated runs, and delivered physically interpretable results. This work establishes harness engineering as a systematic approach to automating CP modeling workflows while maintaining physical interpretability and auditability through visible reasoning traces.

items.title: Cross-Domain Transfer of Depression Voice Biomarkers Depends on the Outcome Instrument: Leakage-Controlled Cross-Sectional Evaluation Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Voice-based depression screening is commercializing rapidly, yet whether voice biomarkers generalize across clinical settings is largely untested. Generalization is usually framed as a question about populations, but it is also a question about the outcome instrument a model is scored against, an effect confounded with other between-study differences in the literature. Objective We tested whether depression voice biomarkers transfer between perinatal and general-psychiatric speech in both directions under strict leakage control and whether transfer depends on the screening instrument. Methods In a cross-sectional, online US study, 390 pregnant participants at a mean of 22 (SD 1) weeks’ gestation (analytical sample n=316) participated in 446 sessions; each participant provided 4 voice recordings and completed the modified 8-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-8) and modified 9-item Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (mEPDS-9). We extracted 375 acoustic descriptors and 330-dimensional Population Dynamics Foundation Model community-health embeddings. Discrimination area under the curve (AUC) was assessed under leakage-controlled cross-validation, with feature and classifier selection inside training folds only and a permutation negative-control harness, across a prespecified grid of 4 speech tasks×4 outcome definitions. The prenatal-trained model was applied to 2 general-psychiatric corpora (Distress Analysis Interview Corpus–Wizard-of-Oz, n=189; Extended Distress Analysis Interview Corpus, n=219) under pure held-out inference, and the open-source Kintsugi Depression/Anxiety Model (DAM), trained on 35,000 individuals, was applied to all 3 cohorts without refitting, with Benjamini-Hochberg multiplicity control. Results In the prenatal cohort, the preregistered outcome was at chance (AUC 0.494, 95% CI 0.431-0.560); no cell in the 16-cell grid survived adjustment under either modeling paradigm. The prenatal-trained model did not transfer to either general-psychiatric corpus (AUCs 0.505 and 0.478). Reverse transfer depended on the screening instrument. The DAM reached an AUC of 0.706 to 0.708 on general-psychiatric speech. In the same participants, it performed at chance against the PHQ-8 (AUC 0.510, 95% CI 0.411-0.609) but discriminated against the mEPDS-9 (AUC 0.645, 95% CI 0.541-0.744), a paired difference of 0.135 (95% CI 0.019-0.248; unadjusted post hoc P =0.02). Exploratory item-level analysis suggests a mechanism: the DAM tracked affective-distress items (crying r =0.26, sadness r =0.21, and overwhelmed r =0.20) but not somatic PHQ-8 items; only crying survived adjustment across 17 tests. Transfer varied by elicitation task (pregnancy narrative 0.653, 95% CI 0.550-0.753; open-ended speech 0.597, 95% CI 0.486-0.699; scripted reading 0.544, 95% CI 0.434-0.651), though these were not formally compared. Conclusions Cross-domain comparison showed a compound shift: population, elicitation task, and outcome instrument differed together, while only the instrument could be varied on its own. Whether a depression voice biomarker transfers may depend not only on the population but also on whether the outcome instrument captures what the model can detect. Validation should state the population, elicitation task, and outcome instrument together; a tool validated against one instrument should not be assumed to work against another.

items.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
items.abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

items.title: Deploying a Control-Logic LLM Assistant in Air-Gapped Power Plants: Lessons in Source Authority and Bounded Retrieval
items.abstract: Deploying Large Language Model (LLM) assistants in industrial operational technology environments poses constraints largely absent from cloud applications: site policies restrict engineering and operational data from leaving the plant, on-premises compute is limited, and incorrect causal attribution can mislead incident response. We report lessons from deploying a control-logic evidence layer that underpins a broader on-premises operator assistance system at two gas power plants. Two prototypes revealed where generative models added avoidable uncertainty and cost. The first used a Vision Language Model (VLM) to reconstruct control topology from PDF printouts routinely exchanged by engineers. Across the full 6,979-page document, extraction reached 0.51 connection precision and required 3.1 hours on 4xH200 GPUs; consultation with controls engineers then revealed a native structured export from the authoring system. The second used an LLM tool-calling agent to plan repeatedly over eight predefined graph operations. In a controlled benchmark of 40 template-generated questions, replacing this agent with explicit execution plans reduced mean token use by 20x and median latency by 3x, with identical retrieved node sets across repeated runs. The deployed design ingests the authoritative export into a versioned knowledge graph, executes bounded graph operations in fixed software, and confines the local LLM to fallback intent classification and evidence-grounded explanation. At one site, the graph contains 221K nodes across seven controllers. Our experience suggests a practical division of labor for high-consequence AI: LLMs interpret natural-language requests and explain results, while deterministic software constructs and retrieves technical evidence grounded in authoritative sources. Abstention, entity disambiguation, graph versioning, and read-only integration provide additional safeguards.

items.abstract: The respectful disposal of damaged Quranic texts presents a crucial socio-religious and environmental management issue for Islamic religious authorities. In Malaysia, the DepartmenThe respectful disposal of damaged Quranic texts presents a crucial socio-religious and environmental management issue for Islamic religious authorities. In Malaysia, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) guidelines specify controlled burning as an approved method. However, existing disposal incinerators operated by state authorities, such as Jabatan Agama Islam Melaka (JAIM), face significant operational issues, including excessive toxic smoke emissions, ergonomic limitations, ash loss due to wind scattering, and performance degradation from 300 kg/day to 150 kg/day after two years. This study presents the design, Finite Element Analysis (FEA), and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation of a redesigned 304 stainless steel Al-Quran disposal incinerator. Concept selection using the Pugh Matrix identified an optimized design incorporating an air blower, smoke filter, dust compartment, and hydraulic lift table. CFD simulations demonstrate that forced aeration elevates internal combustion temperature from 617 °C (blower off) to 1,725 °C (blower on), increasing thermal efficiency and reducing total burning time for 150 kg of paper to under 24 hours. Static FEA using the Von Mises Yield Criterion indicates that while the structure safely supports 300 kg under ambient conditions (FOS = 1.0), thermal stresses at 1,725 °C limit the safe structural payload to 150 kg (FOS = 1.1). To mitigate high-temperature sensitization (425–870 °C) and intergranular corrosion, protective enamel or Ni-Cr composite coatings are evaluated. items.title: Designing Cognitive Scaffolds for Generative-AI-Assisted Introductory Programming
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can make introductory programming tasks easier to complete, but a working program is not evidence of durable learning. This conceptual-theoretical paper integrates research on cognitive load, metacognition, self-explanation, productive failure, appropriate reliance on automation, and recent studies of AI-assisted programming to propose a five-phase cognitive-scaffolding framework. Learners first make an unaided attempt, request bounded assistance, verify the response against requirements and independently designed tests, explain the mechanism and calibrate confidence, and then complete a related transfer task as support fades. AI literacy, ethical disclosure, privacy, and instructor orchestration operate across all phases. The framework identifies process evidence that remains inspectable when generated code is available, including problem representations, hypotheses, verification records, explanations, confidence judgments, and unaided transfer. It also states six testable propositions and an evaluation blueprint for introductory programming courses. The contribution is a bounded design logic, not a claim that the sequence has already been validated: GenAI should reduce avoidable burden while leaving consequential decisions, checks, and explanations with the learner.

items.title: Designing metacognitive scaffolding in flipped learning to enhance students’ visual–spatial reasoning: Evidence from geometry instruction
items.abstract: The development of students’ visual–spatial reasoning is a persistent challenge in geometry learning, where abstract representations and spatial transformations require high levels of cognitive engagement. Although flipped learning has been widely implemented to promote active learning, its effectiveness largely depends on the quality of instructional design and pedagogical support provided during in-class activities. This study investigates how metacognitive scaffolding can be intentionally designed and embedded within flipped learning to enhance students’ visual–spatial reasoning. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed in secondary geometry instruction involving 62 students assigned to experimental and control groups. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and post-tests of visual–spatial reasoning, while qualitative data were obtained from classroom observations and semi-structured teacher interviews. The results indicate that students who experienced metacognitive scaffolding within a flipped learning environment demonstrated significantly greater gains in visual–spatial reasoning than those in a conventional flipped classroom, with a large effect size. Qualitative findings further reveal that scaffolding prompts supported students’ planning, monitoring, and reflective evaluation during problem-solving activities. Overall, the findings suggest that flipped learning environments become more cognitively productive when structured metacognitive scaffolding is deliberately incorporated into the learning design.

items.title: Development and User-Centred Evaluation of a 3D-Printed Assistive Tool for Vehicle Fuel Cap Opening
items.abstract: Opening a vehicle fuel cap can be challenging for individuals experiencing reduced hand strength, impaired motor control, or upper-limb functional limitations because the task requires secure gripping and rotational force. This preliminary study aimed to develop and evaluate 3D-printed assistive-tool concepts for vehicle fuel-cap manipulation using a user-centred approach involving end users and occupational therapy (OT) professionals. Four initial design concepts were developed, of which two prototypes were selected for user evaluation. The prototypes were demonstrated with support from the Rehabilitation Department of Hospital Taiping and evaluated using a structured five-point Likert-scale instrument. Eleven end-user respondents and four OT professionals participated in the evaluation. End users assessed ease of use, ergonomics, effectiveness, safety, and user satisfaction, while OT professionals assessed clinical suitability, ergonomics, safety, functional benefit, and potential for practical application. The end-user group produced overall mean scores of 3.96 for Design 1 and 4.04 for Design 2, indicating generally favourable perceptions of both prototypes and a marginally higher rating for Design 2. OT professionals provided a higher overall rating for Design 1 (5.00) than Design 2 (3.63). Qualitative feedback highlighted the need for improved hand support, grip security, handle configuration, and fuel-cap engagement. The differing evaluations between end users and OT professionals suggest that stakeholder perspectives should be considered concurrently during early-stage assistive-device development. The findings support the feasibility of using 3D printing to rapidly develop task-specific assistive-tool prototypes, while the current results should be interpreted as preliminary rather than evidence of clinical effectiveness. Future work should incorporate objective measurements of grip force, rotational torque, task completion time, mechanical durability, and compatibility with different fuel-cap geometries.

items.title: Development of a Modular, Wheelchair-Accessible Desk Using Design Thinking and User-Centered Design (UCD).
items.abstract: Conventional desks are designed around fixed dimensions and lower structural elements that can hinder frontal approach, reach, and comfortable posture for wheelchair users, limiting their participation in study and work activities. This study aimed to develop a modular and accessible desk concept for wheelchair users through Design Thinking and User-Centered Design. An applied, mixed-methods, descriptive-propositive approach was followed, structured in the five phases of Design Thinking: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and test. In the empathize phase, a questionnaire with two five-point Likert scales (perceived difficulty and importance of desk features) was administered to ten people, six wheelchair users and four non-users, selected through non-probability sampling. Data were analyzed descriptively, and internal consistency was estimated with Cronbach’s alpha. Both scales showed high internal consistency (α = 0.955 and 0.929). The greatest difficulties were plugging in devices and maintaining posture during long periods, while height adjustment, removable storage modules, and ample work surface were the most valued features (mean = 4.20). These findings informed a design brief, a conceptual sketch, and a three-dimensional model of an L-shaped desk with adjustable height, removable storage modules, device charging, and open space for frontal approach. The project is currently at the three-dimensional modeling stage; a physical prototype has not been built, and usability, stability, and ergonomic tests with users remain pending. Because of the small sample and the preliminary nature of the instrument, the results are exploratory and support the relevance of the proposed features rather than confirming the effectiveness of the desk. Future work will build the prototype and evaluate it with a larger group of wheelchair users.

items.title: Development of an HPLC Analytical Method Based on Large Language Models:A Case Study of the Eczema External Wash Formula
items.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas feature complex chemical compositions, and their HPLC quality control method development is time-consuming and experience-dependent. Large language models (LLMs) provide a promising strategy for intelligently assisting analytical method construction. Taking the Eczema External Wash Formula as the research object, this work constructed a human-machine collaborative workflow involving intelligent recommendation, experimental validation and iterative optimization for HPLC method development. Among five prompt strategies tested, expert-role setting with structured reasoning performed best. After inputting formula information, the LLM proposed five chromatographic schemes. Through experimental screening and optimization, the final HPLC method used a SunShell C18 column, mobile phase of 0.1% aqueous formic acid-acetonitrile for gradient elution, with seven markers separated within 55 min. Twenty components were characterized by LC-MS. The validated method exhibited satisfactory linearity, precision, repeatability, stability and recovery. This indicates LLMs can reduce the workload of chromatographic condition exploration and boost the development efficiency of TCM formula analytical methods, supporting intelligent TCM quality control.

items.title: Digital enablement and employee performance in society 5.0: a dual-path model of motivation and exhaustion
items.abstract: Introduction Society 5.0 integrates advanced digital technologies with human-centered work systems, yet its implications for sustainable employee performance remain underexplored. Drawing on Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this study examines the relationship between Society 5.0 enablement intensity (S5EI) and sustainable human performance through autonomous motivation and emotional exhaustion, considering human-centric governance capability as a moderator. Methods The study employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyse data collected from 519 employees working in digitally intensive sectors in India. Results The findings indicate that S5EI is positively associated with sustainable human performance, primarily through autonomous motivation. Emotional exhaustion partially offsets this positive effect through competitive mediation. Human-centric governance capability strengthens the relationship between autonomous motivation and sustainable human performance but does not significantly buffer the negative effect of emotional exhaustion. Discussion The findings conceptualize digital enablement as a dual-valence work condition that simultaneously strengthens autonomy-based motivation and increases digital demands, integrating Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory. The study highlights the importance of participatory digital governance, workload management, and employee recovery measures for supporting sustainable human performance.

items.title: Digital Literacy Of Nursing Students In Clinical Teaching: A Scoping Review Protocol
items.abstract: In an education increasingly mediated by smart technologies, it is essential that nursing students maintain critical thinking and autonomous clinical judgment. Digital literacy goes beyond technical expertise, incorporating an ethical, conscious, and contextualized analysis of the social, political, and epistemological impacts of artificial intelligence. This competence prevents the uncritical use of digital tools and fosters an understanding of their mechanisms, risks, and limitations, including biases and misinformation. In the context of nursing, this approach ensures that technology complements human judgment without compromising safety and person-centered care. Thus, training should be guided by ethical principles, critical reflection, and professional responsibility, preparing future nurses for an increasingly complex and digital clinical landscape. The study participants are nursing students in a clinical teaching setting. The review will follow the JBI methodology and reporting according to PRISMA-ScR. The databases to be searched include CINAHL Plus Complete, MEDLINE Complete Plus, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by unpublished literature in the ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Citation Index (via Web of Science) and RCAAP. Studies in Portuguese, English, and Spanish will be included. Two independent reviewers will perform the analysis, extraction, and synthesis of data using the Rayyan platform. The results will be presented narratively, with tables or figures.

items.title: Digital Transformation Through a Socio‐Technical Systems Lens: Women Leaders' Approaches to Technological Change and Organizational Dynamics
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Organizations navigating digital transformation face persistent challenges integrating social and technical elements to support innovation and worker wellbeing. Despite increasing workforce participation, women remain underrepresented in senior leadership roles that shape how this integration occurs, leaving perspectives shaped by gendered organizational experience underexplored within digital transformation research. Drawing on thematic analysis of interviews with sixteen senior women leaders across Australian organizations, this study applies socio‐technical systems theory and a gender‐informed leadership perspective to examine how these leaders understood and navigated the relationship between technical and social domains during digital transformation. Participants treated technical and social considerations as mutually constitutive, enacting their integration through communication, employee participation, human‐centered work design, capability development and ongoing adaptation. Psychosocial safety emerged across technical, social and integration‐focused accounts as a system‐level condition implicated in this process. Together, these findings provide an empirical account of human‐centric transformation within Industry 5.0 and extend socio‐technical systems theory by conceptualizing integration as an enacted process through which technical and social considerations continually shape one another. A gender‐informed analysis further demonstrates the value of gendered organizational experience for understanding how socio‐technical integration is accomplished in practice.

items.title: Disaggregated LLM Inference in Space: A Communication Feasibility Study
items.abstract: Orbital data centers could enable large-scale AI inference, but efficiently serving a frontier language model to many users may require several compute satellites to cooperate over optical links. While disaggregated inference, which splits large language model (LLM) serving across machines, is well established in terrestrial data centers, its viability under the unique constraints of orbital deployments remains an open question. This article investigates how link capacity and satellite separation affect two types of disaggregated LLM serving, in both compact satellite formations and distributed constellations. Prefill-decode disaggregation (PDD) migrates a large KV cache once per request, while attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) exchanges small activations at every mixture-of-experts layer for every generated token. The two respond to distance in different ways. PDD is limited mainly by link capacity and, with fast enough links, tolerates separations of up to a thousand kilometers. AFD is limited mainly by propagation delay, which accumulates layer by layer and forces attention and expert instances within about a kilometer of each other. Based on these results, we propose a hierarchical orbital inference architecture and provide network design guidelines for future orbital data centers, including the role of ground access latency.

items.title: Distúrbios Musculoesqueléticos em Colaboradores de Contact Center: Prevalência e Estratégias de Prevenção Fisioterapêutica na Empresa Ucall (Angola, 2025)
items.abstract: Introdução: O sector de contact center constitui um dos pilares da economia digital, mas impõe aos seus colaboradores riscos ergonómicos e psicossociais elevados, decorrentes da imobilidade prolongada, da repetitividade gestual e da pressão por indicadores de desempenho. Na empresa Ucall, em Angola, a incidência de Distúrbios Musculoesqueléticos Relacionados ao Trabalho (DORT) constitui um desafio relevante à saúde ocupacional. Objetivo: Analisar a prevalência dos distúrbios musculoesqueléticos e discutir estratégias de prevenção fisioterapêutica em colaboradores de contact center na empresa Ucall, no primeiro semestre de 2025. Metodologia: Estudo descritivo, de abordagem mista (quantitativa e qualitativa) e corte transversal, realizado na empresa Ucall (Talatona, Luanda). A amostra, não probabilística e por conveniência, foi composta por 22 colaboradores de uma população de 80. Os dados foram recolhidos remotamente via Google Forms, com recurso ao Questionário Nórdico de Sintomas Osteomusculares (QNSO) e à Escala Visual Analógica (EVA). Resultados: Identificou-se um paradoxo estrutural: embora 72,7% dos postos de trabalho disponham de cadeiras com ajuste técnico, apenas uma minoria dos colaboradores adota posturas adequadas. A coluna lombar (31,8%) e a região dorsal (18,2%) concentraram a maior prevalência de queixas, com níveis médios de dor entre 6 e 8 na escala EVA em quase metade da amostra. A pressão por metas influenciou a tensão muscular em 77,3% dos inquiridos, e 59,1% classificaram as pausas laborais como apenas ligeiramente satisfatórias. Conclusões: A prevalência elevada de DORT na empresa Ucall exige uma estratégia multidimensional de prevenção fisioterapêutica, que integre ergonomia física, gestão da carga mental e educação postural desde a admissão, consolidando a fisioterapia ocupacional como elemento estratégico para a sustentabilidade da saúde no trabalho. Palavras-chave: Distúrbios Musculoesqueléticos; Prevalência; Contact Center; Fisioterapia Ocupacional; Ucall; Angola. ABSTRACT Introduction: The contact center sector is a pillar of the digital economy, but it exposes employees to elevated ergonomic and psychosocial risks arising from prolonged immobility, repetitiveness, and pressure related to performance indicators. At the Ucall company, in Angola, the incidence of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WRMSD) constitutes a relevant occupational health challenge. Objective: To analyze the prevalence of musculoskeletal disorders and to discuss physiotherapeutic prevention strategies among contact center employees at the Ucall company, in the first semester of 2025. Methods: A descriptive study with a mixed quantitative-qualitative approach and a cross-sectional design was conducted at the Ucall company (Talatona, Luanda). The non-probabilistic, convenience sample consisted of 22 employees drawn from a population of 80. Data were collected remotely via Google Forms, using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ) and the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). Results: A structural paradox was identified: although 72.7% of workstations were equipped with technically adjustable chairs, only a minority of employees adopted adequate posture. The lumbar spine (31.8%) and thoracic region (18.2%) concentrated the highest prevalence of complaints, with mean pain levels between 6 and 8 on the VAS scale in nearly half of the sample. Pressure for targets influenced muscular tension in 77.3% of respondents, and 59.1% rated work breaks as only slightly satisfactory. Conclusions: The high prevalence of WRMSD at Ucall requires a multidimensional physiotherapeutic prevention strategy integrating physical ergonomics, mental workload management, and postural education from onboarding, consolidating occupational physiotherapy as a strategic element for workplace health sustainability. items.title: Do Embedding-Map Distances Guide LLM Ideation? Four Tests Against What Came Next
items.abstract: A popular ideation recipe treats an embedding map of existing work as a guide: pick points far from everything and decode them into ideas. I test four ways such distances could guide ideation against what appeared later. (1) Far random directions are not text: no later item reaches a raw cosine above about 0.10 with one (after centring or whitening, 22 of 24 cells stay out of reach), and an LLM decoder shown a target's neighbours, with score-only feedback, writes those neighbours in all six target sets. A neighbour-free search writes coherent text at median cosine 0.57 and 0.47 to interior gaps, beating the nearest existing item on 15 and 14 of 20, but only 0.07 and 0.06 to far points. (2) On k-means cells of a past-only map, the registered hole score mostly tracks cell size and position; three density-based gap scores forecast which cells grow fastest at or below chance (AUC 0.30 to 0.66) and add nothing to momentum in Steam and arXiv, with patents inconclusive; more isolated new Steam games are slightly better reviewed. (3) LLM continuations of arXiv papers stay closer to the source than papers that cite it, under three user prompts and against proposal rewrites (gpt-4o) and April-December 2023 papers (OLMo). Critique lengthens this step beyond content-free revision, replicated on 150 new papers. Revealing a real follow-up's title turns the ideas by 0.032 along a follow-up-specific direction beyond revision; reviewer, oracle and distance feedback add 0.13, 0.08 and 0.34 of that turn (upper bounds 0.46, 0.46, 0.70), and their turn is not separable from revision or their longer step. (4) For inspiration material graded by distance, no inverted U was detected, on an anticipation margin that tracks format more than content. Original tests were registered before running, follow-ups (thirteen requested in two AI-agent reviews) after the main results; all are dated only by local git commits.

items.title: Does Generative AI Reduce Mental Effort at The Expense of Deep Thinking? An Experimental Investigation of Cognitive Load and Knowledge Retention
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has transformed learning practices, raising critical concerns regarding its influence on cognitive engagement, analytical reasoning, and knowledge retention. This study experimentally examines whether GenAI-assisted learning reduces cognitive load at the expense of deep thinking and sustained knowledge acquisition. A randomized controlled experimental design was employed involving 120 undergraduate students, randomly assigned to an experimental group utilizing ChatGPT (n = 60) and a control group completing equivalent learning activities without AI assistance (n = 60). Participants undertook analytical reading, conceptual problem-solving, and critical reasoning tasks under standardized experimental conditions. Cognitive load was measured using a mental effort rating scale, deep thinking was assessed through rubric-based analytical reasoning evaluations, and knowledge retention was examined using immediate and delayed post-tests administered two weeks apart. Results revealed significantly lower perceived cognitive load among AI-assisted learners (M = 3.42, SD = 1.11) compared with the control group (M = 5.76, SD = 1.24), t(118) = 10.88, p < .001. Conversely, students learning without AI demonstrated superior deep-thinking performance (M = 78.40, SD = 9.65) relative to AI-assisted participants (M = 70.25, SD = 10.82), p < .001. Immediate knowledge retention scores showed comparatively modest differences between the experimental and control groups (82.30% versus 80.10%, respectively). However, delayed retention assessments revealed a substantial performance advantage for the control group (74.60%) over AI-assisted learners (65.20%), indicating greater knowledge deterioration following AI-supported learning. These findings suggest that although GenAI effectively reduces perceived mental effort during academic tasks, such efficiency gains may coincide with diminished analytical engagement and weaker long-term knowledge retention. The study extends cognitive load theory and cognitive offloading perspectives by identifying a potential trade-off between immediate learning efficiency and sustained cognitive development. The findings underscore the importance of pedagogically structured GenAI integration that encourages independent reasoning, active knowledge construction, and meaningful cognitive engagement rather than passive dependence on AI-generated responses. Implications for instructional design, assessment practices, and responsible AI adoption in higher education are discussed.

items.title: Dynamic Thematic Map Generation from Multi-Source Post-Earthquake Data Based on Large Language Models
items.abstract: Within the golden 72 h after an earthquake, the rapid generation of emergency thematic maps is critical for disaster assessment and rescue decision-making, yet it faces core challenges such as the difficulty of reusing experience from historical earthquakes and the weak association among multi-source heterogeneous data. The spatial hallucination inherent in conventional spatial RAG systems can further mislead situational awareness of the affected region and increase decision risk. To address these issues, this paper proposes an adaptive dynamic thematic map generation method that fuses LLMs with Graph RAG for earthquake emergency scenarios. At the knowledge reconstruction level, a dual-channel association constraint mechanism over spatial and semantic channels is designed to link base geographic data, emergency resources, and historical cases across modalities, thereby constructing a directed heterogeneous event-region-resource spatial knowledge graph and achieving spatially grounded semantic consolidation of heterogeneous spatiotemporal multi-source data in emergency scenarios. At the retrieval and reasoning level, asymmetric query rewriting and multi-dimensional parallel recall over graph topology are introduced together with causal constraints of earthquake-triggered spatiotemporal propagation and proactive circuit breaking, which upgrades the text matching of conventional RAG to multi-hop spatiotemporal causal reasoning over the entire cross-domain chain of earthquake emergency response, suppresses spatial hallucination at the source of spatial decision making, and ensures the rigor of historical case reuse. At the collaborative mapping level, a multi-dimensional text fusion model of evolutionary evidence chains is constructed, which converts the discrete reasoning results of the LLM into standardized structured semantics and realizes mechanism-driven mapping of disaster semantics such as seismic intensity and lifeline engineering damage onto emergency thematic map layers. In addition, in-memory and distributed multi-level caching strategies are introduced to reduce the computational response latency when massive data floods in after strong earthquakes. Experiments on real earthquakes such as the Lushan and Luding events show that the proposed method raises the layer match rate to 0.791 (versus 0.295 for the strongest baseline), achieves the best layer-set F1 (0.252), reduces the in-window viewport-center displacement to 21.2 km, and attains a blind-judged semantic accuracy of 0.429 over the full 200-query set (0.881 on in-window queries) against 0.00 for all baselines, while a spatially filtered hybrid baseline reaches only 0.068. Driven by a lightweight 7B model, the cold-start generation of a single thematic map takes only 0.83 min, and the dynamic viewport refresh is kept within 12 s when the cache is activated, which meets the time window requirement for rapid post-earthquake map production. Given the moderate overall semantic accuracy and the disclosed out-of-graph coverage boundary, the method is positioned as an efficient and verifiable decision-support solution whose outputs still require human verification, rather than as a fully autonomous cartographic product.

items.title: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
items.abstract: After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M. Through benchmarking and failure analysis, we identify a practical challenge that some cases are inherently difficult to predict in real-world settings. To address this, we introduce decision model-based gating to filter out cases where predictions are unlikely to be correct before they are presented to the user. Our trained model outperforms existing decision models and raises pass@5 among shown suggestions by 12--25 points at a gating threshold. Our code is available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation.

items.title: Effect of Facilitated Problem-Based Learning on Intrinsic and Extrinsic Motivation Among Nursing Students in North-East Nigeria
items.abstract: This study investigated the effect of facilitated Problem-Based Learning (PBL) on intrinsic and extrinsic motivation among nursing students in North-East Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pre-test, post-test control group design was adopted. The population comprised 1,065 ND II nursing students from six Colleges of Nursing Science in North-East Nigeria, from which 200 students were selected using a multi-stage sampling procedure. The sample consisted of 100 students in the experimental group exposed to facilitated PBL and 100 students in the control group taught using conventional lecture-based instruction. Data were collected using a 28-item Academic Motivation Questionnaire (AMQ). The instrument demonstrated satisfactory reliability with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of 0.84. The experimental group participated in a six-week facilitated PBL intervention involving nursing-related case scenarios, guided questioning, collaborative learning, feedback, and self-directed learning activities. Data were analyzed using means, standard deviations, and t-tests at the 0.05 level of significance. Finding showed that the experimental group recorded an increase in mean intrinsic-motivation scores from 26.30 at pre-test to 50.30 at post-test, compared with an increase from 25.90 to 30.20 in the control group. A significant effect was also found on extrinsic motivation, with the experimental group recording a greater reduction in extrinsic motivation than the control group, t(198) = 8.72, p < .05. therefore, motivation also differed significantly between the facilitated PBL and lecture groups, t(198) = 14.02, p < .001. Furthermore, a significant difference was observed between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, t(198) = 6.85, p < .001. The study concluded that facilitated PBL is an effective instructional approach for strengthening intrinsic motivation and promoting more self-directed learning among nursing students. It was recommended that nursing institutions should integrate facilitated PBL into their programmes, train educators in effective PBL facilitation, provide adequate learning resources, and emphasize learning activities that foster students’ intrinsic motivation.

items.title: EFFECTS OF VIRTUAL REALITY AND GAMIFICATION ON MOTOR FUNCTION AND TREATMENT ADHERENCE IN POST-STROKE PATIENTS: A LITERATURE REVIEW
items.abstract: Considering that stroke is one of the main causes of physical disability worldwide, with more than 60% of survivors presenting residual motor impairment, and that conventional physical therapy imposes limitations on repetitiveness and adherence, the objective is to analyze the efficacy of virtual reality (VR) and gamification in the physical therapy rehabilitation of post-stroke patients, emphasizing motor function and treatment adherence. Therefore, a narrative/integrative literature review of a descriptive-analytical nature is carried out, with qualitative synthesis of evidence, performed in the BVS/LILACS, SciELO, PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar databases, with an adapted PICO strategy, DeCS/MeSH descriptors and free terms, between 2015 and 2025, in Portuguese and English, which resulted in the inclusion of 18 studies organized into two thematic axes. Thus, it is observed that VR, especially when associated with conventional physical therapy, promotes consistent benefits on upper limb motor function, balance, gait and coordination, with small to moderate effect sizes (SMD 0.32; 95% CI 0.08–0.56) and moderate to low certainty of evidence, and that gamification favors adherence and engagement by increasing intrinsic motivation, although the evidence for this outcome is scarcer and heterogeneous. This allows concluding that VR and gamification are promising and complementary resources to conventional physical therapy, with documented benefits on motor function and relevant potential for treatment adherence, and that Brazilian randomized clinical trials with standardized protocols and validated adherence measurement instruments are recommended.

items.title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study
items.abstract: We audit instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog. The research question we answer with this experiment is which models disclose a protected secret embedded in the system prompt, and through which techniques. Each model guards a secret 16-character flag set in its system prompt, while an artificial intelligence (AI) agent (OpenCode, powered by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), steered by a human researcher, tries to persuade it to emit the flag. The flag was exfiltrated from 296 of the 363 models, plus four models released after the initial catalog freeze, for 300 captures in total. Of these, 170 involved a non-English language pivot, most often French. Each capture shows that a model ranked a user request above its system instruction at least once. It does not show that the model provably resists untested attacks, nor that it would consistently leak semantically sensitive data, nor that it is vulnerable to harmful-content jailbreaks. For practitioners, we draw three lessons: do not store secrets in system prompts, enforce critical behavior outside the model with output validation and deterministic checks, and do not let a large language model (LLM) judge be the sole decider of consequential outcomes.

items.title: Emerging Research Fronts in Public Relations Scholarship: An Analytical Synthesis of Technological Disruption, Epistemic Diversification, and Disciplinary Self-Examination
items.abstract: This paper presents an analytical synthesis of contemporary research fronts in public relations (PR) scholarship, drawing on recent work in leading journals (Public Relations Review, Journal of Public Relations Research, Corporate Communications: An International Journal), agenda-setting signals from disciplinary bodies (ICA, IPR, PRSA), and 2025–2026 special-issue programs. Seven interrelated research fronts are identified: (a) artificial intelligence adoption, ethics, and disciplinary disruption; (b) disinformation, trust, and organizational resilience; (c) theoretical and methodological pluralism, including de-Westernization; (d) employee communication, advocacy, and internal activism; (e) crisis spillover and contagion; (f) measurement, evaluation, and predictive analytics; and (g) bibliometric self-mapping. The analysis argues that these fronts are shaped by three macro-level forces—technological disruption, epistemic diversification, and disciplinary self-examination—and that the intersections among them constitute the field’s most promising publication spaces. Drawing on recent empirical evidence, including a 277-agency survey of AI adoption across the Arab world (Koa et al., 2025), a longitudinal analysis of 630 fact-checks of disinformation targeting organizations in Spain (Rodríguez Fernández et al., 2026), and a dedicated special issue on crisis spillover (Laufer & Wang, 2024), the synthesis shows that the field’s most successful emerging work does not abandon established PR theory but redeploys it in new empirical territories. The paper concludes with a maturity–opportunity assessment and a strategic map of research gaps to guide manuscript positioning in Q1/Q2 outlets during the 2026–2027 publication cycle.

items.title: Emotionally Aware AI Chatbots for Adolescents: A Review of Psychological Principles for Learning, Calibrated Trust, and Healthy Human–AI Interaction
items.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence now belongs to ordinary adolescent life, but the psychological research that should guide its design spreads over fields which seldom cite each other. Research on adolescent development, on misinformation susceptibility, on trust in automation, on chatbot-supported learning and on companion-chatbot overreliance has grown up separately, and each of these areas answers only part of the question of how a general-purpose chatbot should talk to a teenager. This paper brings together twenty-one sources from developmental psychology, human factors, human-computer interaction and educational technology, in order to show what is now known about adolescent chatbot interaction and what this means for conversational design. Three results appear repeatedly in this research. First, adolescence is a design context of its own, not a smaller version of adulthood, since reward sensitivity, social influence and emotional regulation are still developing, while exposure to persuasive conversational systems has already reached almost everyone. Second, trust in a chatbot changes behavior in ways that can be measured; thus, the proper design target is calibrated trust rather than maximal trust. Third, the failure modes that matter most for adolescent users, that is, hallucination, sycophancy and unwarranted confidence, originate in the model; the user is not their source. From these results this paper consolidates ten conversational design principles into four clusters, namely epistemic calibration, metacognitive scaffolding, bounded emotional support and autonomy preservation. The framework here is a conceptual synthesis and puts forward testable predictions, but it has not been empirically validated.

items.title: Energy-harvesting wearable patch for real-time athletes’ risk detection
items.abstract: Athletes are often at high risk of sudden and severe injury or illness during training sessions due to a lack of safety measures. Failure to monitor health conditions and vital signs during training can result in serious consequences for athletes. Currently, several devices in the market measure vital signs and provide them as raw data; however, they do not prioritize the athlete’s safety and often offer limited feedback on their health condition. Additionally, many of these devices lack ergonomic designs, which limit the athlete’s mobility. This wearable health monitoring device was designed to be both lightweight and cost-effective. It collects and tracks health metrics while providing real-time feedback to the user via an application to support the athlete’s safety. A key feature is the utilization of energy harvesting technology to power the system, which includes a heart rate sensor, core body temperature sensor, and sweat sensor. Furthermore, the acquired data are analyzed using a developed algorithm to detect abnormal and critical health conditions such as dehydration, overtraining syndrome, exertional heat illnesses, and heart attacks risk indicators. These critical data points, which exceed normal ranges, are classified into two alarm levels: Warning Level and Critical Level. Ultimately, the data are transmitted via Wi-Fi to a mobile application, which provides information about the athlete’s health status and guidance to ensure their safety.

items.title: Epidemiology of Orthopaedic Surgeon Suicide
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Suicide remains an important occupational health concern among physicians, including orthopaedic surgeons. We aimed to identify the current characteristics and risk factors of suicide among orthopaedic surgeons compared with nonsurgeon physicians. METHODS: The National Violent Death Reporting System database was queried for physician suicides from 2017 to 2022. A total of 746 physician suicides were analyzed. RESULTS: Orthopaedic surgeons had the highest proportion of suicides among surgical subspecialties at 25%, increasing over the study period. White orthopaedic surgeons comprised 100% of these cases, and men comprised 94.4%. Compared with nonsurgeons, risk factors of surgeon suicide included White race (OR 3.32, 95% CI, 1.19 to 9.28) and being married (OR 1.9, 95% CI, 1.09 to 3.32). Documented mental health problems (OR 0.52, 95% CI, 0.31 to 0.87) and depressed mood (OR 0.48, 95% CI, 0.27 to 0.85) seemed inversely associated with surgeon suicide. DISCUSSION: Orthopaedic surgery accounted for the highest proportion of surgeon suicide deaths among specified surgical subspecialties. The inverse association with documented mental health issues could suggest profound underreporting and a pervasive culture of silence among surgeons. Interventions must address systemic stigma preventing surgeons from seeking psychiatric care.

items.title: Ergonomic issues in vertical farming systems: a PRISMA-informed narrative review
items.abstract: Vertical farming (VF) represents a transformative approach to agricultural production utilizing multi-tiered, controlled-environment systems, yet it introduces unique ergonomic challenges distinct from conventional agriculture. This literature review synthesizes current evidence on ergonomic issues in vertical farming systems, alongside evidence from indoor farming and broader controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) systems, examining musculoskeletal disorder (MSD) prevalence, risk factors, assessment methodologies, and intervention strategies. Agricultural workers in greenhouse and indoor farming environments experience MSD prevalence rates of 50.9% to 89.3%, with the lower back, shoulders, knees, and neck most commonly affected. Available evidence suggests that vertical farming may present distinctive ergonomic challenges, including multi-tiered configurations associated with overhead reaching, lower-tier access constraints, repetitive precision tasks, environmental stressors, and complex human-technology interactions. However, much of the current evidence is inferred from greenhouse and broader controlled-environment agriculture systems. While traditional ergonomic assessment tools (RULA, REBA, OWAS) and advanced methods (EMG) have been applied in agricultural contexts, their adaptation to vertical farming remains limited. Current interventions show promise through workspace optimization, tool redesign, automation, and participatory ergonomics approaches. However, significant knowledge gaps persist regarding longitudinal health outcomes, human-automation interaction, cognitive ergonomics, and socioeconomic dimensions specific to vertical farming. This review highlights the emerging need for human-centered design principles in VF system development to ensure worker health, safety, and operational sustainability.

items.title: Ergonomic Setup for Trans‐Radial Procedures Using a Height‐Adjustable Trolley in the Angiography Suite
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Trans-radial access (TRA), while experiencing varying global adoption among interventional radiologists, offers potential benefits including reduced access-site bleeding, accelerated patient ambulation, and decreased overall healthcare expenditures compared with trans-femoral access (TFA). However, TRA introduces distinct occupational ergonomic burdens, including asymmetrical arm abduction, working height discrepancies with standard angiographic tables, and inadequate support for long microcatheters and guidewires. These biomechanical constraints heighten operator fatigue and increase the cumulative risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders. TECHNIQUE: A mobile, height-adjustable trolley-conceptually adapted from ergonomic sit-stand workstations-was integrated into the angiography suite workflow. Arranged parallel to the patient in a Z-shaped spatial configuration, the trolley is linked to the patient's outstretched access arm using an extended sterile drape to establish a stable, continuous sterile working platform. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: This technical configuration restores neutral operator posture, mitigates lumbar torsion and cervical strain, eliminates sterile field breaches from suspended equipment, and increases the physical working distance from primary scatter radiation sources. Furthermore, the elevated surface facilitates gravity-assisted administration of dense Yttrium-90 microspheres during radioembolization and prevents rotational interference during cone-beam computed tomography acquisitions. CONCLUSION: The implementation of a height-adjustable trolley provides a simple, cost-effective, and highly adaptable ergonomic solution that optimizes procedural efficiency, sterile field integrity, and radiation safety during trans-radial interventional procedures.

items.title: Ergonomics-Integrated Generative AI for Personalized Work Design in Aging and Diversifying Industrial Workforces
items.abstract: In industrialized countries, rapid population aging and declining birth rates have made labor shortages a critical issue in industrial workplaces. Without actively utilizing elderly workers, persons with disabilities, and foreign workers, on-site operations risk becoming unsustainable. Addressing this challenge requires not only technological innovation but also a transdisciplinary engineering approach that integrates human, social, and industrial system perspectives. This study proposes a personalized work design framework that combines generative artificial intelligence (AI) and ergonomics to enable inclusive and sustainable industrial operations. The proposed framework utilizes individual attribute data—such as age-related physical characteristics, functional limitations, work experience, and language proficiency—to generate task configurations tailored to diverse worker groups. Ergonomic principles are systematically embedded into the generative AI model to adapt task sequences, work postures, workload distribution, and operational instructions according to individual capabilities and constraints. From an engineering perspective, the framework integrates data-driven AI modeling, human factors engineering, and production system design to dynamically optimize the interaction between workers and industrial environments. A case study conducted in a manufacturing-related setting demonstrates that the proposed approach reduces physical strain and cognitive workload while maintaining or improving productivity and operational stability. The results indicate that AI-driven ergonomic task personalization is particularly effective in enabling the participation of elderly workers, persons with disabilities, and foreign workers in on-site industrial work. This research highlights the value of transdisciplinary engineering in addressing complex societal challenges posed by demographic change. By bridging generative AI, ergonomics, and industrial engineering, the proposed framework provides a scalable and human-centered solution for designing adaptive workplaces and supporting long-term workforce sustainability in aging and diversifying societies.

items.title: Evaluating Authorization and Trust Boundaries in Agentic Orchestration Frameworks
items.abstract: Agentic AI systems extend large language models with tools, memory, and multi-agent collaboration, introducing security risks at orchestration boundaries. These risks depend on how identities are represented, operations are authorized, and instructions or information propagate between components. We evaluate LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, and OpenClaw through twelve experiments mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications using a common LLM (gpt-4o-mini). The experiments cover prompt injection, unauthorized resource access and command execution, memory poisoning, and inter-agent trust and identity attacks. Adversarial inputs induced unauthorized tool invocation, while tool chaining, stale filesystem validation, encoded instructions, and inter-agent delegation exposed weaknesses in authorization across component boundaries. Memory poisoning showed that untrusted state can influence responses, a risk distinct from conventional access-control violations. In the evaluated protected configurations, explicit authorization, controlled capability assignment, filesystem containment, and execution safeguards prevented specific unauthorized operations. The findings emphasize preserving authorization and information-trust boundaries throughout agentic workflows rather than treating framework capabilities or model-level instructions as sufficient security guarantees.

items.title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings. Although sentiment analysis is a common task in this area, affective meaning in social media discourse is often conveyed through culturally situated and pragmatically indirect cues that are not well captured by label-centric evaluation alone. In this paper, we evaluate the robustness of LLMs for sentiment analysis of Spanish political discourse from social media, with emphasis on culturally situated affective interpretation. We introduce a diagnostic protocol that combines three independent human annotation views into Gold and Ambiguous subsets, and extends the corpus with a Synthetic subset built from sentiment-flipped counterfactuals selected through model-conditioned perplexity and LLM-as-a-judge criteria. Using this framework, we compare proprietary and open-weight models under zero-shot and few-shot prompting, focusing on predictive robustness across human agreement conditions and counterfactual shift. Our results show that annotation ambiguity and counterfactual perturbation reveal failure modes that conventional evaluation on the original corpus tends to obscure. GPT-4.1-mini remains the most stable among the evaluated models, whereas the two smaller open-weight models degrade more markedly under synthetic perturbations, and few-shot prompting provides only limited gains. Overall, the paper contributes a reproducible protocol for robustness-oriented evaluation in political sentiment analysis, an empirical characterization of model behavior under ambiguity and sentiment-flipped counterfactuals, and a publicly available Spanish social media dataset with three-way human sentiment annotations.

items.title: Evaluating large language models for quality control in research ethics review
items.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) could streamline research ethics and governance review by automating routine quality control checks. This study assessed Claude 3.5 Sonnet, ChatGPT4o, and Microsoft CoPilot in evaluating participant information sheets against Health Research Authority standards. Six clinical trial applications were processed using 32 standardised queries, with accuracy, processing time, error rates, and response quality assessed by two blinded reviewers. Claude showed the highest accuracy, detected more deviations from guidance, and had the fastest processing time (7.17 ± 0.68 min vs. ChatGPT 13.58 ± 2.2 min, CoPilot 23.25 ± 6.21 min). Hallucination rates were lowest in Claude, followed by ChatGPT and CoPilot. Claude also received the highest response quality ratings (77.6% “very good” vs. ChatGPT 56.7%, CoPilot 45.2%). While all three models were capable, Claude consistently outperformed the others, demonstrating the potential of LLM-assisted quality control while emphasizing the need for human oversight.

items.title: Evaluation Metrics and Frameworks for Knowledge Graphs in Nursing: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence and big data drive the intelligent transformation of healthcare, Knowledge Graphs (KGs) have emerged as a pivotal technology for clinical decision support and medical knowledge discovery. However, as an independent discipline, nursing faces unique ontological challenges in KG construction, characterized by high data heterogeneity and significant contextual dependency. The current lack of a systematic evaluation framework makes it difficult to assess both construction quality (intrinsic evaluation) and clinical effectiveness (extrinsic evaluation), which not only hinders scientific appraisal but also risks patient safety due to potential decision-making errors. This scoping review aims to clarify the theoretical foundations and distinct characteristics of Nursing Knowledge Graphs (NKGs), systematically mapping evaluation dimensions across the entire lifecycle from data extraction to knowledge fusion. By establishing a rigorous search strategy and research framework, this project provides the methodological groundwork for a standardized nursing knowledge evaluation system, ensuring the accuracy, safety, and clinical utility of nursing AI applications.

items.title: Evidence Diet: When Graph Evidence Helps LLMs Rank Competing Candidates
items.abstract: When several candidates have graph support, does it matter which candidate receives which supporter and path counts? We study how LLM rankers use collaborative evidence on Amazon Books and MovieTV. Swapping user-level evidence degrades ranking, while matched item substitutions have little effect. On fixed clean-trained checkpoints, unrelated catalog text lowers Hit@1 from 44.77% to 38.70%, with 99.9% of rankings still valid. Across all three paired seeds, the NDCG@5 difference between count and path prompts was larger after count training than after path training. Degree matching preserves target paths while giving more rivals support. Across the full degree-matched development pools, adding candidate-level graph records to history improves NDCG@5 by 2.28 points on Books and 2.54 on MovieTV. When the target and a rival both have support, path- and count-trained rankers benefit from retaining counts. On these development queries, adding counts numerically to history scores outperforms presenting them as text. For count-trained rankers, exchanging intact count pairs among supported candidates preserves support and token length, yet lowers NDCG@5 by 4.06 points on 141 Books queries and 3.26 on 104 MovieTV queries. A frozen evaluation on 274 previously unused Books users with supported targets and rivals confirms the attribution effect: correct assignment improves pairwise accuracy by 6.07 percentage points (95% CI [4.18, 8.00]).

items.title: Exploring user experience design for third restrooms: from inclusive perspective
items.abstract: Third restrooms assist the elderly, young children, and people with mobility impairments. As a key service hub in public spaces, their indoor design directly impacts user satisfaction, yet unmet diverse needs hinder the experience. This study developed a four-stage, eight-activity inclusive design framework. Integrating the AEIOU–Kano model, it compared international standards and conducted field research visiting 20 third restrooms across China. Focusing on five typical user groups—families with young children, caregivers of the elderly, wheelchair users, people with visual impairments, and people with temporary disabilities—the study identified needs and established an evaluation indicator system. It then proposed optimization solutions for spatial layout and facility configuration, validated using Jack simulation. Results indicate the integrated model effectively supports need identification and design decisions, and simulations verified ergonomic adequacy across different body types. These findings provide theoretical and practical foundations for the ergonomic optimization and inclusive design of third restrooms in public spaces, offering guidance for an inclusive service system within public spaces.

items.title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
items.abstract: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets. We present FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions. Following the Jev formulation, FaceJev answers eight independent questions about facial parts using a shared image encoding and reads anomaly probabilities from the native answer logits. A face is classified as forged if any part is predicted to be abnormal, directly linking the detection result to the part decisions. We construct PartForensics, a dataset of approximately 160k images with binary anomaly targets for the eight facial parts, to supervise these decisions. We further propose FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards. FaceJev outperforms the strongest baseline by 7.25 percentage points on unseen manipulations. Extensive ablation studies validate our design choices and the effectiveness of the main components.

items.abstract: This article analyzes the Knowledge Lighthouse, the name Petrobras gives to the knowledge management practice commonly known as Yellow Pages. The solution is a business intelligence dashboard that integrates corporate data and professional records to locate expertise by knowledge area or by person. A qualitative and descriptive approach was adopted through a single case study and bibliographic and documentary analysis. The theoretical framework combines knowledge management, transactive memory, competence mapping, intellectual capital, communities of practice, and sociotechnical systems. The study describes the dashboard’s conception, its SAP/SIRH data sources, daily D-1 updating, search and profile detail views, query paths, and corporate access. The analytical findings indicate that the solution may improve expert findability, reduce search costs, foster learning and knowledge integration, and support critical knowledge management, team formation, innovation, internal mobility, succession, and organizational memory. Its effectiveness, however, depends on a governed taxonomy, complete and current data, trust, participation, workflow integration, data protection, and value-oriented evaluation. The study concludes that the Knowledge Lighthouse should operate as an infrastructure for discovery and connection, complemented by human validation and linked to communities, repositories, and knowledgetransfer practices, rather than being converted into an automatic employee assessment mechanism.

items.title: FMint-SDE: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Accelerating Numerical Simulation of SDEs via Error Correction
items.abstract: Abstract. Fast and accurate simulation of dynamical systems is a fundamental challenge across scientific and engineering domains. Traditional numerical integrators often face a trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency, while existing neural network–based approaches typically require training a separate model for each case. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel multimodal foundation model for large-scale simulations of differential equations: FMint-SDE (Foundation Model based on Initialization for stochastic differential equations). Based on a decoder-only transformer with in-context learning, FMint-SDE leverages numerical and textual modalities to learn a universal error-correction scheme. It is trained using prompted sequences of coarse solutions generated by conventional solvers, enabling broad generalization across diverse systems. We evaluate our models on a suite of challenging SDE benchmarks spanning applications in molecular dynamics, mechanical systems, finance, and biology. Experimental results show that our approach achieves a superior accuracy-efficiency tradeoff compared to classical solvers, underscoring the potential of FMint-SDE as a general-purpose simulation tool for dynamical systems. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and Data Available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SISC and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://github.com/margotyjx/FMint-SDE and in the supplementary materials ( M181717_Supplementary_Materials_1.pdf [7.87MB], FMint-SDE-main.zip [206KB]), linked from the main article webpage. items.title: Formally verified harness for Shor's order finding algorithm with $O(n^{2+ε})$ gate cost
items.abstract: It is commonly understood that factoring a general $n$-bit biprime via Shor's order finding algorithm requires $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ gates by leveraging schoolbook integer arithmetics for addition and multiplication. Recent developments in quantum arithmetic circuits leveraging recursive Toom-Cook schemes have improved the cost scaling to $O(n^{2+ε})$. Here $ε>0$ depends on algorithm implementation details of the recursive multiplication steps, which allow for a vast number of design choices. The challenge in navigating such design space also presents an opportunity for demonstrating innovative practices in quantum software engineering in the era of open agentic science. We present a formally verified harness that ingests a design specification (namely a "policy" that describes a recursive circuit design scheme) from an external source, which may be an AI agent, and produces a set of formalized proofs covering mathematical correctness of the algorithm implementation, asymptotic scaling of the end-to-end gate cost, as well as the correctness of translating the verified algorithm to a detailed circuit implementation with an intermediate representation. The harness is published as an open challenge where human researchers and AI agents can search for more efficient factoring circuits while retaining machine-checked guarantees of correctness and end-to-end asymptotic complexity.

items.title: From Apology to Action: Apologies, Compensation, and Cooperation in LLM Agents
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can make decisions that affect other agents, but what happens after a harmful or unsuccessful interaction remains poorly understood. We investigate whether apologies by LLM agents are associated with subsequent cooperative behaviour, using controlled Prisoner's Dilemma experiments with four commercial models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Mistral Large 3). Across payoff conditions, we examine when agents apologise, the reasons they provide, and the actions that follow. We also examine how access to one round of interaction history affects behaviour and, in a second experiment, whether and how agents offer compensation alongside their apologies. Apology behaviour differed substantially across models and preceding interaction outcomes, and verbal expressions of cooperation did not always align with subsequent actions. Notably, Claude Opus 4.8 apologised even after mutual cooperation, while Mistral Large 3 apologised after being exploited but continued to defect even when its opponent cooperated. After unilateral defection, positively compensated apologies from GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro were followed by mutual cooperation, unlike those from Claude and Mistral. Our findings suggest that apologies, compensation, and strategic behaviour are distinct: conciliatory messages may precede continued defection, while costly apologies may go unanswered. This has important implications for the study of machine behaviour and human-AI interactions, as verbal signals alone may not reliably reflect an AI system's subsequent actions.
